newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens aims to expand its use of Internet.
newsitem.headline: Siemens aims to expand its use of Internet.

text.p: German industrial group Siemens AG plans to spend at least 500 million marks ($268.3 million) to revamp internal communications and expand the company's use of the Internet.
The company told Reuters it aimed to boost productivity by wiring the company worldwide for e-mail, video conferencing and other forms of electronic communications.

"The idea is to have a knowledged-based company," spokesman Thomas Weber told Reuters. "If you want to be effective as a worldwide company, you have to have a transparent orgaisation. We want to unify the company for multimedia."
Rama Krishnan, formerly head of Siemens Business Services, was named chief information officer, a new position, to lead the project.

The appointment was announced at an earnings news conference last month when chief exeuctive Heinrich von Pierer said he had "some concern" that European companies were falling behind U.S. competitors in using computer technology.
He noted that Germany has six Internet PCs for every 1,000 people, while the U.S. has 23. "Siemens is taking action to correct this situation," he said.

Throughout the rest of the year, Siemens planned to improve the company's communications networks to support video conferencing. It also planned to expand e-mail systems to link all 200,000 employees who use PCs in their jobs.
On the Internet, it would overhaul its sites to make them eaiser to navigate, said Roland Huegel, a spokesman for the online communications project.

The company would also create a restricted area of its internal Internet, or intranet, where Siemens emplolyees, consultants and outside software companies would have a "virtual workspace" to collaborate on the company's new image.

The new online design -- the result of a July meeting of 160 marketing, public relations, sales and technical staffers from around the world -- would enable Internet users to reach any part of Siemens from "www.siemens.com," Huegel said.
"At the moment we have 278 Siemens domains worldwide, and not all of them are linked," he said.

For example, Siemens' U.S. Internet site is not yet linked to sites in Germany. "By January, siemens.com will give people a central access point to all of Siemens," Huegel said. "You will be able to go there and get to the information for any country or any business area."
In addition to revamping the structure of its Internet sites, which include some 45,000 pages of data now, Siemens planned to provide customer services over the Internet.
It would first put thousands pages of product data on the Internet, and later systems that let customers order parts for products such as telephones, fax machines and household appliances.
"We have to move slowly on that because we still have to work with the dealers that distribute our products the traditional way," Huegel said.
